items.stem: In a test run on a polished vertical circular chute of radius 0.875 m, a 1.85 kg precision titanium sphere enters the bottom at 7.2 m s⁻¹ with negligible friction (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the minimum bottom entry speed that would still allow it to complete the full vertical loop without losing contact at the top?
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.8 × 0.875) = 6.55 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: During handling trials on a flat epoxy distribution floor, a 220 kg autonomous warehouse transport robot follows a horizontal circular path of radius 125 m at 16.6 m s⁻¹. Its polyurethane wheels have a static friction coefficient of 0.55 with the track (g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) a_c = v² / r = (16.6)² / 125 = 2.20 m s⁻². (b) Below the skid limit, f_s = m a_c = 220 × 2.20 = 485 N. (c) Maximum non-skidding speed v_max = √(μ_s g r) = 26.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies mass by centripetal acceleration (rather than using limiting μ_s mg).
Equates m v_max² / r to μ_s mg.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the centripetal acceleration of the autonomous warehouse transport robot.
Determine the magnitude of the sideways static frictional force acting on the polyurethane wheels at this speed.
workingSteps: Since the autonomous warehouse transport robot does not skid, static friction supplies the required centripetal force.

parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum speed at which the autonomous warehouse transport robot can negotiate this curve without skidding.
workingSteps: At the skid limit, m v_max² / r = μ_s m g.

items.stem: The blackbody continuum of a evolved red-clump giant (radius 1.51 × 10¹⁰ m, distance 5.23 × 10¹⁶ m) corresponds to an effective photospheric temperature of 5930 K as recorded by an astrometric space mission. Take Wien's constant b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K. At what wavelength, in nm, does its emitted spectrum peak?
items.workedSolution: Using Wien's displacement law, λ_max = b / T = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / 5930 = 4.89 × 10⁻⁷ m = 489 nm.

items.stem: Six-month baseline observations (1 AU radius) with a stellar intensity interferometer yield parallax p = 0.571 arcsec for a bright southern-sky reference star radiating 2.21 × 10²⁹ W (1 pc is the distance at which a 1 AU baseline subtends a parallax angle of 1 arcsecond, so d / pc = 1 / (p / arcsec)). Given 1 pc = 3.26 ly, how many light-years away is the star?
items.workedSolution: Distance in parsecs d = 1 / p = 1 / 0.571 = 1.75 pc. Converting to light-years gives d = 1.75 × 3.26 = 5.71 ly.

items.stem: A 3.5 kg acrobatic drone tether pod revolves at a constant speed of 4.44 m s⁻¹ in a vertical circle of radius 1.35 m guided by a constant-speed vertical line. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension at the highest point of the circle?
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both tension and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 3.5 × ((4.44)² / 1.35 − 9.81) = 16.8 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 16.8 N.

items.stem: Engineers testing rotational instrumentation in a guidance-sensor test chamber whirl a 0.6 kg sphere on the end of a 1.8 m tether. Throughout the motion, the tether makes a constant semi-vertical angle of 20 ° with the vertical axis. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 20° = (0.6)(9.8) gives T = 6.26 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 1.8 sin 20° = 0.616 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.48 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 2.61 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

items.stem: An autonomous orbital servicing tug of mass 320 kg initially orbits a dense terrestrial world (mass 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) in a circular orbit of radius r₁ = 7.57 × 10⁶ m. Propulsion burns transfer it into a higher coaxial circular orbit of radius r₂ = 1.21 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Initial bound energy E_tot(r₁) = −GMm/(2r₁) = -8.42 × 10⁹ J. (b) Final bound energy E_tot(r₂) = -5.27 × 10⁹ J, so ΔE_tot = 3.15 × 10⁹ J. (c) Outer orbital period T₂ = 2π√(r₂³/GM) = 1.33 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Kepler's third law at outer radius r₂.

parts.prompt: Calculate the initial total mechanical energy of the autonomous orbital servicing tug in the orbit of radius r₁.
Determine the minimum mechanical energy that must be supplied to transfer the autonomous orbital servicing tug into the circular orbit of radius r₂.
Calculate the orbital period of the autonomous orbital servicing tug in the outer circular orbit of radius r₂.

items.stem: In a gas-giant moon pair along their line of centres of centre-to-centre separation 5.57 × 10⁸ m, Major Moon (mass 1.04 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Minor Moon (mass 2.12 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) are modelled as airless non-rotating spheres with V_g = 0 at infinity (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Null point distance x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 4.87 × 10⁸ m. (b) Combined scalar potential V(x₀) = -1.63 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. (c) Potential barrier from x = R₁ to x₀ is ΔV = 1.07 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹, giving v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.46 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀).
Equates ½v_min² to potential barrier V(x₀) − V(R₁).

items.stem: Assuming uniform internal density throughout a spherical basaltic terrestrial planetoid of mass 2.21 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 1.08 × 10⁷ m, find the gravitational field strength experienced by a 508 kg orbital transponder at interior radius 2.7 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Inside a uniform sphere (r < R), enclosed mass M_enc = M(r/R)³, so g(r) = G M r / R³ = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.21 × 10²⁴ × 2.7 × 10⁶) / (1.08 × 10⁷)³ = 0.316 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates gravitational field strength at r = 2.7 × 10⁶ m to obtain 0.316 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: A deep-shaft gravimeter of mass 900 kg is located at radial distance 3.15 × 10⁷ m from the centre of an airless synthetic uniform planetary body of mass 2.63 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 7.01 × 10⁶ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and potential to be zero at infinity, what is the gravitational potential at the deep-shaft gravimeter's position?
items.workedSolution: Outside the spherical mass, V_g = −G M / r = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.63 × 10²⁵) / 3.15 × 10⁷ = -5.57 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_g = −GM / r = -5.57 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ including the negative sign.

items.stem: A 952 kg inter-moon cargo ferry coasts along the axis connecting Host World (mass 5.36 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Icy Moon (mass 7.54 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m) in a super-Earth and its captured icy satellite of centre-to-centre separation 3.05 × 10⁸ m, crossing coordinate x = 1.68 × 10⁸ m from Host World's centre (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 2.22 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 1.68 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.00999 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 9.51 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 9.51 N.

items.stem: Engineers design a superelevated guideway curve with a horizontal curve radius of 72 m and banking angle 25 ° so that a 320 kg carriage corners in a horizontal plane with zero sideways friction (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 25° = mg gives N = 3.46 × 10³ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 25° = 1.46 × 10³ N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 18.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the carriage.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the carriage.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 18.1 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the low-redshift recession speed (in km s⁻¹) of a lenticular field galaxy whose neutral Sodium D absorption doublet shifts from 589 nm to 626.7 nm. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and H₀ = 73.5 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: z = Δλ / λ₀ = (626.7 − 589) / 589 = 0.0640. In the low-redshift regime, v ≈ z c = 0.0640 × 3.00 × 10⁵ km s⁻¹ = 1.92 × 10⁴ km s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v ≈ (Δλ / λ₀) c to obtain 1.92 × 10⁴ km s⁻¹.

items.stem: A X-ray timing observatory of mass 1350 kg moves in a circular orbit of radius 3.3 × 10⁷ m around a central rocky exoplanet of mass 2.99 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 7.86 × 10⁶ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and zero potential energy at infinity. What is the total mechanical energy of the spacecraft in this orbit?
items.workedSolution: In a circular orbit, E_k = +GMm/(2r) and E_p = −GMm/r, so E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.99 × 10²⁴ × 1350) / (2 × 3.3 × 10⁷) = -4.08 × 10⁹ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r) with negative sign to obtain -4.08 × 10⁹ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_tot = −GMm/(2r), quoting gravitational potential energy −GMm/r instead.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the negative bound-state sign, reporting +GMm/(2r) instead of −GMm/(2r).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits both the negative sign and the virial factor of 1/2, reporting +GMm/r.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Stefan-Boltzmann scaling to obtain 0.0107 R☉.

items.stem: An unpowered frictionless coaster bogie of mass 0.2 kg enters the bottom of an inverted steel loop-the-loop of radius 0.6 m with horizontal speed 5.96 m s⁻¹. Resistive forces are negligible; take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 3.46 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 2.04 N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 5.42 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the frictionless coaster bogie as it passes the highest point of the loop.
workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the string tension acting on the frictionless coaster bogie at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: Safety engineers specify an unbanked wet-asphalt roundabout of radius 90 m for a 760 kg proving-ground test saloon travelling at 13.5 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.81 m s⁻², calculate the minimum static friction coefficient needed.
items.workedSolution: No-skid cornering requires μ_s m g ≥ m v² / r, so μ_min = v² / (g r) = (13.5)² / (9.81 × 90) = 0.206.

Calculate the total luminosity of the star.

items.stem: Using a 1 AU orbital baseline, an optical interferometry array measures an annual parallax angle of 0.18 arcsec for a eclipsing-binary primary component of total luminosity 4.6 × 10²⁹ W (1 pc is the distance at which a 1 AU baseline subtends a parallax angle of 1 arcsecond, so d / pc = 1 / (p / arcsec)). Take 1 pc = 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 1 / 0.18 = 5.56 pc. (b) In SI units, d = 1.71 × 10¹⁷ m. (c) Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = 1.25 × 10⁻⁶ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies distance in parsecs by 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m pc⁻¹.
Applies inverse-square law b = L / (4π d²).

Convert this stellar distance into metres.

items.stem: Motorized drive control keeps a 0.75 kg mass moving at constant tangential speed 5.56 m s⁻¹ around a vertical circular path of radius 1.4 m using an inextensible tether. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Critical apex speed v_min = √(gR) = 3.71 m s⁻¹. (b) At the top, F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 9.20 N. (c) At the bottom, F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 23.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Sets support force to zero at apex so mg = m v_min² / R.
Subtracts mg from m v² / R at the top.
Adds mg to m v² / R at the bottom.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the highest point required for the tether to remain taut.
workingSteps: Setting support force at the top to zero gives m v_min² / R = mg.

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the cord when the mass passes through the highest point at 5.56 m s⁻¹.
workingSteps: At the top, F_top + mg = m v² / R.

parts.prompt: Determine the tension in the cord when the mass passes through the lowest point at 5.56 m s⁻¹.
workingSteps: At the bottom, F_bot − mg = m v² / R.

items.stem: Swinging steadily around a vertical axis in an overhead cable rig, a 1.2 kg suspended ice-arena tracking camera pod hangs from a 1.1 m tether inclined at 42 ° to the vertical (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is its speed along the circular path?
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.1 sin 42° = 0.736 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.736 × tan 42°) = 2.55 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.55 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Between circular orbits of radii r₁ = 1.26 × 10⁷ m and r₂ = 2.52 × 10⁷ m around a uniform spherical planet (mass 1.1 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 5.72 × 10⁶ m), a 463 kg planetary gravity-mapping orbiter coasts along a tangent Hohmann transfer ellipse (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²). Calculate the transit time from periapsis to apoapsis.
items.workedSolution: The transfer ellipse has semi-major axis a = ½(r₁ + r₂) = 1.89 × 10⁷ m. Coasting from periapsis to apoapsis takes half an orbital period: t_H = π√(a³ / GM) = 9.53 × 10³ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses a = ½(r₁ + r₂) and t_H = π√(a³ / GM) to obtain 9.53 × 10³ s.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Takes half the outer circular period using r₂ instead of the transfer ellipse semi-major axis (r₁ + r₂)/2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the full elliptical period 2π√(a³ / GM) instead of the half-orbit Hohmann coast time π√(a³ / GM).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses major axis (r₁ + r₂) instead of semi-major axis a = (r₁ + r₂)/2 in Kepler's third law.

items.stem: Determine the net scalar gravitational potential (zero at infinity) at the collinear saddle point of zero field between Major Moon (4.42 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Minor Moon (1.77 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m), whose centres lie 5.89 × 10⁸ m apart (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 4.91 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -7.21 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -7.21 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Inside a uniform-density basaltic terrestrial planetoid of total mass 2.69 × 10²⁵ kg and surface radius 4.92 × 10⁶ m, a 123 kg orbital transponder takes gravimetric readings at r = 3.2 × 10⁶ m from the centre. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Surface field g₀ = GM/R² = 74.1 N kg⁻¹. (b) At r = 3.2 × 10⁶ m, uniform-sphere interior scaling g = g₀(r/R) gives 48.2 N kg⁻¹. (c) Force on probe F = mg = 5.93 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes M and R into g₀ = GM / R².
Applies linear interior field law g(r) = GMr/R³.
Multiplies probe mass by field strength at r.

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational field strength at the surface of the basaltic terrestrial planetoid.
Determine the gravitational field strength at the orbital transponder's radial position r = 3.2 × 10⁶ m.
workingSteps: For a uniform sphere with r < R, g(r) = g₀ (r / R) = G M r / R³.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the gravitational force acting on the 123 kg orbital transponder at this position.

items.stem: Relative to zero potential at infinity, the gravitational potential curve of a spherical metal-enriched exoplanet (mass 6.95 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 8.76 × 10⁶ m) is sampled by a 952 kg atmospheric-skimming bus at radial coordinate 3.94 × 10⁷ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -5.29 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 1.03 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 3.94 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -1.12 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_g = −GM / R with negative sign.
Applies E_p = −GMm / r at probe radius.

Hence, or otherwise, determine the escape speed from the surface of the metal-enriched exoplanet.
workingSteps: ½ m v_esc² + m V_surface = 0 => v_esc = √(−2 V_surface).

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the 952 kg atmospheric-skimming bus at r = 3.94 × 10⁷ m.

items.stem: In a gas-giant moon pair along their line of centres, Major Moon (mass 5.07 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Minor Moon (mass 3.17 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.74 × 10⁶ m) have a centre-to-centre separation of 3.46 × 10⁸ m. At what distance from the centre of Major Moon along the line joining their centres is the resultant gravitational field strength zero?
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 2.77 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 2.77 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: A 1750 kg alpine highway tour bus corners at 16.1 m s⁻¹ on a superelevated mountain bend of horizontal radius 58 m banked at 14 °, where the static friction coefficient is 0.4 (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed at which it can round this banked turn without skidding outward?
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 14° + 0.4 cos 14°) / (cos 14° − 0.4 sin 14°)] = 20.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 20.2 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Light collected from a receding compact starburst dwarf galaxy reveals the doubly ionized Oxygen forbidden line shifted from λ₀ = 500.7 nm to λ_obs = 510.06 nm. Use c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and Hubble constant H₀ = 66 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) z = (λ_obs − λ₀)/λ₀ = 0.0187. (b) Recession speed v ≈ zc = 5.61 × 10³ km s⁻¹. (c) Hubble distance d = v/H₀ = 85.0 Mpc.

items.stem: Mission tracking places a 1180 kg X-ray timing observatory at height 1.4 × 10⁷ m above a central rocky exoplanet of mass 1.78 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 5.4 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²). Calculate the circular orbital speed.
items.workedSolution: Orbital radius from planet centre r = R_p + h = 5.4 × 10⁶ + 1.4 × 10⁷ = 1.94 × 10⁷ m. Equating GMm / r² = mv² / r gives v = √(GM / r) = √(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 1.78 × 10²⁵ / 1.94 × 10⁷) = 7.82 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = 1.94 × 10⁷ m to obtain 7.82 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Referenced to zero potential energy at infinity, the orbital energy diagram models a 931 kg synthetic-aperture radar satellite circling a spherical terrestrial planet (mass 2.15 × 10²⁵ kg, surface radius 5.33 × 10⁶ m) at radius r = 2.24 × 10⁷ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k = GMm/(2r) = 2.98 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) E_p = −GMm/r = -5.96 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Total mechanical energy E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = -2.98 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_p = −GMm / r including negative sign.
Sums E_k + E_p or applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of the synthetic-aperture radar satellite in this circular orbit.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = G M m / r², E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r).

workingSteps: E_tot = E_k + E_p = −G M m / (2r) = -2.98 × 10¹⁰ J.

items.stem: Four benchmark stars from a parallax-calibrated stellar evolution atlas are displayed on a Hertzsprung–Russell diagram without region labels. For Star Eta, T = 18500 K and L = 0.008 L☉. Use L☉ = 3.83 × 10²⁶ W, R☉ = 6.96 × 10⁸ m, and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) Star Eta lies in the white-dwarf region. (b) L = 0.008 × 3.83 × 10²⁶ = 3.06 × 10²⁴ W. (c) R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 6.06 × 10⁶ m = 0.00871 R☉.

markScheme.criterion: Applies R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] and divides by R☉.

items.stem: Coasting without friction, a 1.85 kg gravity-fed capsule car passes the lowest point of a circular vertical inversion loop (radius 4.32 m) at 16.9 m s⁻¹ where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate its speed as it crosses the apex.
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((16.9)² − 4 × 9.81 × 4.32) = 10.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 10.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A track-cycling sprinter of mass 1150 kg travels at a constant speed of 24.7 m s⁻¹ along the flat warm-up apron inside a velodrome of radius 105 m. The coefficient of static friction between its tubular tyres and the ground is 0.88. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) a_c = v² / r = (24.7)² / 105 = 5.81 m s⁻². (b) Below the skid limit, f_s = m a_c = 1150 × 5.81 = 6.68 × 10³ N. (c) Maximum non-skidding speed v_max = √(μ_s g r) = 30.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies mass by centripetal acceleration (rather than using limiting μ_s mg).
Equates m v_max² / r to μ_s mg.

Determine the magnitude of the sideways static frictional force acting on the tubular tyres at this speed.
workingSteps: Since the track-cycling sprinter does not skid, static friction supplies the required centripetal force.

parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum speed at which the track-cycling sprinter can negotiate this curve without skidding.
workingSteps: At the skid limit, m v_max² / r = μ_s m g.

items.stem: The blackbody continuum of a nearby M-dwarf flare star (radius 1.55 × 10¹⁰ m, distance 1.56 × 10¹⁶ m) corresponds to an effective photospheric temperature of 18400 K as recorded by a cooled CCD radiometer. Take Wien's constant b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K. At what wavelength, in nm, does its emitted spectrum peak?
items.workedSolution: Using Wien's displacement law, λ_max = b / T = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / 18400 = 1.58 × 10⁻⁷ m = 158 nm.

items.stem: Across Earth's 1 AU semi-major orbital baseline, an ultraviolet sky survey records an annual stellar parallax of 0.125 arcsec for a hot B-type Orion-association star of luminosity 4.6 × 10²⁸ W (1 pc is the distance at which a 1 AU baseline subtends a parallax angle of 1 arcsecond, so d / pc = 1 / (p / arcsec)). Using 1 pc = 3.26 ly, calculate the distance in light-years.
items.workedSolution: Distance in parsecs d = 1 / p = 1 / 0.125 = 8.00 pc. Converting to light-years gives d = 8.00 × 3.26 = 26.1 ly.

items.stem: In a vertical whirl boom of radius 0.65 m, a 0.75 kg aerospace g-tolerance capsule rotates vertically at 3.69 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², if the drive is slowed, at what critical apex speed does the tension vanish?
items.workedSolution: At critical contact at the top, tension = 0 so weight alone provides centripetal force: mg = m v_min² / R => v_min = √(g R) = √(9.81 × 0.65) = 2.53 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets top support force to zero to obtain v_min = √(gR) = 2.53 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In an inertial navigation testbed, a gyroscopic reference mass of mass 1.2 kg is suspended from a fixed ceiling pivot by a light inextensible cord of length 0.95 m. The reference mass moves at constant speed in a horizontal circle such that the cord maintains a steady angle of 24 ° to the vertical. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 24° = (1.2)(9.8) gives T = 12.9 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 0.95 sin 24° = 0.386 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.30 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 1.87 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

parts.prompt: Determine the linear speed of the reference mass along its horizontal circular path.
workingSteps: Horizontal radius r = L sin θ = 0.95 sin 24° = 0.386 m.
From T sin θ = m v² / r, v = √(g r tan θ) = 1.30 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A ultraviolet spectroscopy satellite of mass 1200 kg initially orbits an airless rocky planet (mass 1.91 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 8.52 × 10⁶ m) in a circular orbit of radius r₁ = 1.19 × 10⁷ m. Propulsion burns transfer it into a higher coaxial circular orbit of radius r₂ = 4.28 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Initial bound energy E_tot(r₁) = −GMm/(2r₁) = -6.42 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) Final bound energy E_tot(r₂) = -1.79 × 10¹⁰ J, so ΔE_tot = 4.64 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Outer orbital period T₂ = 2π√(r₂³/GM) = 4.93 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Kepler's third law at outer radius r₂.

items.stem: Mission planners analyse ballistic transfers across a double-planetesimal binary system where Body Alpha (8.84 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Body Beta (1.38 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) are separated by 4.17 × 10⁸ m between centres. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and zero potential at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) Null point distance x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.71 × 10⁸ m. (b) Combined scalar potential V(x₀) = -1.79 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. (c) Potential barrier from x = R₁ to x₀ is ΔV = 7.87 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹, giving v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.25 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀).
Equates ½v_min² to potential barrier V(x₀) − V(R₁).

workingSteps: Equating field magnitudes gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.71 × 10⁸ m.

workingSteps: V(x₀) = −G M₁ / x₀ − G M₂ / (d − x₀) = -1.79 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

workingSteps: ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 7.87 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹; v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.25 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Model a charted extrasolar rocky world as a sphere of uniform density with total mass 3.38 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 5.9 × 10⁶ m. A magnetospheric probe of mass 370 kg descends along a radial borehole to distance 2.36 × 10⁶ m from the planet's centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². What is the gravitational field strength at this interior point?
items.workedSolution: Inside a uniform sphere (r < R), enclosed mass M_enc = M(r/R)³, so g(r) = G M r / R³ = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 3.38 × 10²⁴ × 2.36 × 10⁶) / (5.9 × 10⁶)³ = 2.59 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates gravitational field strength at r = 2.36 × 10⁶ m to obtain 2.59 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Two spherical bodies in an asteroidal binary pair — Primary Asteroid (6.32 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Secondary Moonlet (7.02 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.74 × 10⁶ m) — lie 4.26 × 10⁸ m apart between centres while a 1690 kg ion-beam shepherd craft is located 1.49 × 10⁸ m from Primary Asteroid's centre along their joining line. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.20 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 1.49 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.0184 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 31.1 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 31.1 N.

workingSteps: At the null point, G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)².
Taking square roots gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.20 × 10⁸ m.

workingSteps: |g| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = 0.0184 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: An autonomous mining haul truck of combined mass 880 kg travels around a banked quarry spiral ramp of horizontal radius 58 m inclined at a constant banking angle of 16 ° to the horizontal. At the chosen design speed, zero lateral frictional force acts along the slope. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 16° = mg gives N = 8.97 × 10³ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 16° = 2.47 × 10³ N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 12.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the truck.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the truck.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 12.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In an extragalactic survey with H₀ = 69.5 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, the ionized Calcium H absorption line (rest wavelength 396.8 nm) from a distant Coma-analog galaxy arrives at 404.22 nm. Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the Hubble distance in Mpc.
items.workedSolution: Redshift z = (λ_obs − λ₀) / λ₀ = (404.22 − 396.8) / 396.8 = 0.0187. Recession speed v ≈ z c = 5.61 × 10³ km s⁻¹. From Hubble's law v = H₀ d, d = v / H₀ = 5.61 × 10³ / 69.5 = 80.7 Mpc.

markScheme.criterion: Finds z = 0.0187, v = 5.61 × 10³ km s⁻¹, and d = v / H₀ = 80.7 Mpc.

items.stem: Orbital telemetry tracks a 233 kg ultraviolet spectroscopy satellite maintaining circular motion at height h = 1.89 × 10⁶ m above an airless rocky planet of mass 5.36 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 5.4 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) With orbital radius r = 7.29 × 10⁶ m, g = GM/r² = 6.73 N kg⁻¹. (b) Orbital speed v = √(GM/r) = 7.00 × 10³ m s⁻¹. (c) Period T = 2πr/v = 6.54 × 10³ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses centre-to-centre orbital radius r in g = GM / r².
Applies T = 2πr / v or Kepler's third law.

items.stem: Orbiting a uniform spherical planet (mass 2.09 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 9.78 × 10⁶ m) along a circle of radius 4.11 × 10⁷ m, a planetary gravity-mapping orbiter has mass 1130 kg. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate the orbital kinetic energy of the spacecraft.
items.workedSolution: Since m v² / r = G M m / r², orbital kinetic energy is E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r) = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.09 × 10²⁵ × 1130) / (2 × 4.11 × 10⁷) = 1.92 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assigns a negative sign to kinetic energy by confusing E_k with total orbital energy E_tot.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses surface altitude (r − R_p) instead of orbital radius r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_k = ½mv² = GMm/(2r), computing GMm/r instead.

items.stem: Determine the stellar radius of Star Alpha as a multiple of R☉ given its HR coordinates from an open-cluster Gaia photometric survey: T = 3800 K and L = 180 L☉. Use L☉ = 3.83 × 10²⁶ W, R☉ = 6.96 × 10⁸ m, and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: Luminosity L = 180 × 3.83 × 10²⁶ = 6.89 × 10²⁸ W. From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] = 2.15 × 10¹⁰ m, so R / R☉ = R / (6.96 × 10⁸) = 31.0 R☉.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Stefan-Boltzmann scaling to obtain 31.0 R☉.

items.stem: An unpowered skatepark test trolley of mass 45 kg enters the bottom of a smooth circular vertical cradle of radius 2.5 m with horizontal speed 15.9 m s⁻¹. Resistive forces are negligible; take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 12.4 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 2.34 × 10³ N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 11.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the skatepark test trolley as it passes the highest point of the loop.
workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the skatepark test trolley at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: A Formula-Student electric race car of mass 220 kg negotiates a level dry-tarmac skidpad of radius 90 m at a constant speed of 14.8 m s⁻¹ without skidding. The coefficient of static friction between its slick tyres and the surface is 0.74 (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What lateral frictional force acts on the slick tyres?
items.workedSolution: Because 14.8 m s⁻¹ is below the skidding threshold v_max = √(μ_s g r) = 25.6 m s⁻¹, static friction self-adjusts to match the required centripetal force: f_s = m v² / r = 220 × (14.8)² / 90 = 535 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses f_s = m v² / r (not μ_s mg) to obtain 535 N.

items.workedSolution: (a) λ_max = b/T = 200 nm. (b) L = 4πR²σT⁴ = 6.71 × 10³⁰ W. (c) Apparent brightness b_app = L/(4πd²) = 6.10 × 10⁻⁴ W m⁻².

items.stem: Using a 1 AU orbital baseline, an infrared space observatory measures an annual parallax angle of 0.13 arcsec for a cool K-type giant Aldebaran-analog of total luminosity 4.89 × 10²⁸ W (1 pc is the distance at which a 1 AU baseline subtends a parallax angle of 1 arcsecond, so d / pc = 1 / (p / arcsec)). Take 1 pc = 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 1 / 0.13 = 7.69 pc. (b) In SI units, d = 2.37 × 10¹⁷ m. (c) Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = 6.91 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies distance in parsecs by 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m pc⁻¹.
Applies inverse-square law b = L / (4π d²).

items.stem: In a rotational mechanics rig, an inextensible tether of radius 3.28 m guides a 1.32 kg calibration mass at steady speed 7.37 m s⁻¹ in a vertical plane (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Critical apex speed v_min = √(gR) = 5.67 m s⁻¹. (b) At the top, F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 8.91 N. (c) At the bottom, F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 34.8 N.

markScheme.criterion: Sets support force to zero at apex so mg = m v_min² / R.
Subtracts mg from m v² / R at the top.
Adds mg to m v² / R at the bottom.

workingSteps: Setting support force at the top to zero gives m v_min² / R = mg.

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the cord when the mass passes through the highest point at 7.37 m s⁻¹.
workingSteps: At the top, F_top + mg = m v² / R.

parts.prompt: Determine the tension in the cord when the mass passes through the lowest point at 7.37 m s⁻¹.
workingSteps: At the bottom, F_bot − mg = m v² / R.

items.stem: During rotational testing in an inertial navigation testbed, a 1.8 kg reference mass on a 0.95 m tether describes a horizontal circle with the tether inclined at 24 ° to the downward vertical. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², calculate the tension force in the tether.
items.workedSolution: Vertical equilibrium requires T cos θ = mg, so T = (1.8 × 9.8) / cos 24° = 19.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves T cos 24° = mg to obtain T = 19.3 N.

items.stem: From the airless surface of Primary Planet (mass 1.25 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m), a cislunar transfer probe is fired along the line of centres toward Companion Moon (mass 1.95 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) at separation 2.77 × 10⁸ m. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², determine the threshold launch speed to cross the null-point barrier.
items.workedSolution: Surface potential at x = R₁ is V(R₁) = −GM₁/R₁ − GM₂/(d − R₁) = -1.14 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹. Null-point potential at x₀ = 2.46 × 10⁸ m is V(x₀) = -3.81 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. Potential barrier ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 1.10 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹, so v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.48 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) and v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.48 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Modelling a spherical tidally locked silicate exoplanet (mass 1.25 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 3.5 × 10⁶ m) with constant density throughout, engineers lower a 650 kg descent lander to interior radial distance 8.75 × 10⁵ m from the centre (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).

items.stem: An airless spherical airless iron-core protoplanet has mass 1.31 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 3.19 × 10⁶ m. A reconnaissance craft of mass 780 kg is stationed at radial distance 1.21 × 10⁷ m from the planet's centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and gravitational potential to be zero at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -2.74 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 2.34 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 1.21 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -5.63 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_g = −GM / R with negative sign.
Applies E_p = −GMm / r at probe radius.

Hence, or otherwise, determine the escape speed from the surface of the airless iron-core protoplanet.
workingSteps: ½ m v_esc² + m V_surface = 0 => v_esc = √(−2 V_surface).

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the 780 kg reconnaissance craft at r = 1.21 × 10⁷ m.

items.stem: Along the axis connecting Host World (1.07 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Icy Moon (2.97 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.74 × 10⁶ m) in a super-Earth and its captured icy satellite of separation 5.38 × 10⁸ m, locate the zero-field coordinate measured from the centre of Host World.
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 4.61 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 4.61 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: An Olympic track cyclist of mass 160 kg rounds a Siberian-pine velodrome banking of horizontal radius 32 m banked at 14 ° to the horizontal. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². At what design speed is zero lateral friction required along the slope?
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 32 × tan 14°) = 8.84 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 14°) to obtain 8.84 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A blue emission-line galaxy is observed spectroscopically. The singly ionized Oxygen doublet, which has rest wavelength 372.7 nm in the laboratory, appears at observed wavelength 379.67 nm. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and H₀ = 70 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) z = (λ_obs − λ₀)/λ₀ = 0.0187. (b) Recession speed v ≈ zc = 5.61 × 10³ km s⁻¹. (c) Hubble distance d = v/H₀ = 80.1 Mpc.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies z by c and converts to km s⁻¹.

items.stem: Mission tracking places a 794 kg cryogenic infrared space telescope at height 8.31 × 10⁶ m above a terrestrial host planet of mass 1.39 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 5.54 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²). Calculate the circular orbital speed.
items.workedSolution: Orbital radius from planet centre r = R_p + h = 5.54 × 10⁶ + 8.31 × 10⁶ = 1.385 × 10⁷ m. Equating GMm / r² = mv² / r gives v = √(GM / r) = √(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 1.39 × 10²⁵ / 1.385 × 10⁷) = 8.18 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = 1.385 × 10⁷ m to obtain 8.18 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In a circular orbit of centre-to-centre radius 1.62 × 10⁷ m around a spherical silicate planet (mass 8.84 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 6.23 × 10⁶ m), a 444 kg laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter has E_p = 0 at infinity. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k = GMm/(2r) = 8.08 × 10⁹ J. (b) E_p = −GMm/r = -1.62 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Total mechanical energy E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = -8.08 × 10⁹ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_p = −GMm / r including negative sign.
Sums E_k + E_p or applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of the laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter in this circular orbit.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = G M m / r², E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter.
Determine the total mechanical energy of the laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter.
workingSteps: E_tot = E_k + E_p = −G M m / (2r) = -8.08 × 10⁹ J.

items.stem: Four benchmark stars from a parallax-calibrated stellar evolution atlas are displayed on a Hertzsprung–Russell diagram without region labels. For Star Epsilon-2, T = 6690 K and L = 4.7 L☉. Use L☉ = 3.83 × 10²⁶ W, R☉ = 6.96 × 10⁸ m, and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) Star Epsilon-2 lies in the main-sequence region. (b) L = 4.7 × 3.83 × 10²⁶ = 1.80 × 10²⁷ W. (c) R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 1.12 × 10⁹ m = 1.61 R☉.

markScheme.criterion: Applies R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] and divides by R☉.

items.stem: Conserving mechanical energy throughout a vertical circular guide ring of radius 2.57 m, a 370 kg low-friction maglev test sled enters at the bottom with speed 15.1 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Determine the speed at the summit of the loop.
items.workedSolution: Rising from bottom to top increases height by Δh = 2R. By conservation of energy, ½m v_top² + mg(2R) = ½m v_bot², so v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = √((15.1)² − 4 × 9.8 × 2.57) = 11.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses Δh = 2R in v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) to obtain 11.3 m s⁻¹.

items.workedSolution: (a) a_c = v² / r = (13.5)² / 52 = 3.50 m s⁻². (b) Below the skid limit, f_s = m a_c = 95 × 3.50 = 333 N. (c) Maximum non-skidding speed v_max = √(μ_s g r) = 15.6 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies mass by centripetal acceleration (rather than using limiting μ_s mg).

Determine the magnitude of the sideways static frictional force acting on the rubber tyres at this speed.
workingSteps: Since the electric micro-mobility scooter does not skid, static friction supplies the required centripetal force.

workingSteps: At the skid limit, m v_max² / r = μ_s m g.

items.stem: Determine the radiant flux density b = L / (4πd²) received at a space-based spectrometer from a spherical blackbody luminous F-type subgiant of radius 3.83 × 10⁹ m and surface temperature 6250 K located 4.38 × 10¹⁶ m away (σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴).
items.workedSolution: Luminosity L = 4π R² σ T⁴ = 4π(3.83 × 10⁹)²(5.67 × 10⁻⁸)(6250)⁴ = 1.59 × 10²⁸ W. Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = σ T⁴ (R / d)² = 6.62 × 10⁻⁷ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses L = 4πR²σT⁴ and b = L / (4πd²) to obtain 6.62 × 10⁻⁷ W m⁻².

items.stem: From a high-altitude observatory, a yellow-white standard-candle star has bolometric output 7.1 × 10²⁹ W and annual parallax p = 0.693 arcsec on a 1 AU baseline (1 pc is the distance at which a 1 AU baseline subtends a parallax angle of 1 arcsecond, so d / pc = 1 / (p / arcsec)). Taking 1 pc = 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m, find the radiant flux density arriving at Earth.
items.workedSolution: d = (1 / 0.693) pc = 1.44 pc = 4.45 × 10¹⁶ m. Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = 7.1 × 10²⁹ / (4π × (4.45 × 10¹⁶)²) = 2.85 × 10⁻⁵ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Converts d = (1/p) pc to metres and evaluates b = L/(4πd²) = 2.85 × 10⁻⁵ W m⁻².

items.stem: Telemetry from a vertical circular guide rail of radius 1.1 m shows a 0.9 kg instrumented acrylic sphere whirling in a vertical plane at constant speed 5.19 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², determine the normal contact force at the top.
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both normal contact force and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 0.9 × ((5.19)² / 1.1 − 9.8) = 13.2 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 13.2 N.

items.stem: The diagram represents a 1.4 kg tower-crane suspended ballast block in a steady slewing test describing a horizontal circle while supported by a taut cord of length 2.4 m inclined at 38 ° to the vertical. Take gravitational field strength g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 38° = (1.4)(9.81) gives T = 17.4 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 2.4 sin 38° = 1.48 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 3.37 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 2.76 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

items.stem: A navigation constellation spacecraft of mass 803 kg initially orbits a spherical host world (mass 1.47 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 7.76 × 10⁶ m) in a circular orbit of radius r₁ = 1.09 × 10⁷ m. Propulsion burns transfer it into a higher coaxial circular orbit of radius r₂ = 3.05 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Initial bound energy E_tot(r₁) = −GMm/(2r₁) = -3.61 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) Final bound energy E_tot(r₂) = -1.29 × 10¹⁰ J, so ΔE_tot = 2.32 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Outer orbital period T₂ = 2π√(r₂³/GM) = 3.38 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Kepler's third law at outer radius r₂.

parts.prompt: Calculate the initial total mechanical energy of the navigation constellation spacecraft in the orbit of radius r₁.
Determine the minimum mechanical energy that must be supplied to transfer the navigation constellation spacecraft into the circular orbit of radius r₂.
Calculate the orbital period of the navigation constellation spacecraft in the outer circular orbit of radius r₂.

items.stem: In a terrestrial bi-planetary system of centre-to-centre separation 4.06 × 10⁸ m, Planet Major (mass 1.59 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Planet Minor (mass 1.77 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) are modelled as airless non-rotating spheres with V_g = 0 at infinity (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Null point distance x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.04 × 10⁸ m. (b) Combined scalar potential V(x₀) = -4.65 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. (c) Potential barrier from x = R₁ to x₀ is ΔV = 1.92 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹, giving v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.96 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀).
Equates ½v_min² to potential barrier V(x₀) − V(R₁).

workingSteps: Equating field magnitudes gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.04 × 10⁸ m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined gravitational potential at this null point.
workingSteps: V(x₀) = −G M₁ / x₀ − G M₂ / (d − x₀) = -4.65 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Determine the minimum launch speed from the surface of Planet Major along the line of centres required for a scientific transit module to reach Planet Minor.
workingSteps: ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 1.92 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹; v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.96 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Inside a uniform-density basaltic terrestrial planetoid (mass 5.2 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.33 × 10⁶ m), a 134 kg orbital transponder reaches radial distance 2.93 × 10⁶ m from the planetary centre (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²). Calculate the local gravitational field strength.
items.workedSolution: Inside a uniform sphere (r < R), enclosed mass M_enc = M(r/R)³, so g(r) = G M r / R³ = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 5.2 × 10²⁴ × 2.93 × 10⁶) / (5.33 × 10⁶)³ = 6.71 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates gravitational field strength at r = 2.93 × 10⁶ m to obtain 6.71 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: A spherical charted extrasolar rocky world (mass 1.31 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 9.87 × 10⁶ m) is observed by a 620 kg magnetospheric probe at radial distance 3.16 × 10⁷ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², at what minimum speed must an object leave the surface R to reach infinity?
items.workedSolution: Setting ½m v_esc² − G M m / R = 0 gives v_esc = √(2 G M / R) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 1.31 × 10²⁵ / 9.87 × 10⁶) = 1.33 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates surface escape speed √(2GM / R) = 1.33 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A 1200 kg scientific transit module coasts along the axis connecting Planet Major (mass 7.46 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Planet Minor (mass 2.98 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) in a terrestrial bi-planetary system of centre-to-centre separation 4.61 × 10⁸ m, crossing coordinate x = 2.86 × 10⁸ m from Planet Major's centre (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.84 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 2.86 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.00543 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 6.52 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 6.52 N.

parts.prompt: Calculate the distance from the centre of Planet Major to the collinear point where the resultant gravitational field strength is zero.
workingSteps: At the null point, G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)².
Taking square roots gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.84 × 10⁸ m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant gravitational field strength when the scientific transit module is 2.86 × 10⁸ m from the centre of Planet Major.
workingSteps: |g| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = 0.00543 N kg⁻¹.

parts.prompt: State the magnitude of the resultant gravitational force on the 1200 kg scientific transit module at this point.

items.stem: Engineers design a banked elevated beamway with a horizontal curve radius of 58 m and banking angle 28 ° so that a 1750 kg shuttle corners in a horizontal plane with zero sideways friction (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 28° = mg gives N = 1.94 × 10⁴ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 28° = 9.13 × 10³ N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 17.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the shuttle.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the shuttle.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 17.4 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the redshifted wavelength (in nm) received at Earth for the Magnesium b triplet feature (rest wavelength 517.5 nm) emitted by a giant cD cluster-centre galaxy at distance 75.57 Mpc, taking H₀ = 71.5 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: Recession speed v = H₀ d = 71.5 × 75.57 = 5.40 × 10³ km s⁻¹. Redshift z = v / c = 0.0180, so λ_obs = λ₀(1 + z) = 517.5 × (1 + 0.0180) = 527 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates v = H₀d, z = v/c, and λ_obs = λ₀(1 + z) = 527 nm.

items.stem: A planetary gravity-mapping orbiter of mass 656 kg moves in a circular orbit of radius 1.674 × 10⁷ m around a uniform spherical planet of mass 1.07 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 7.97 × 10⁶ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) With orbital radius r = 1.674 × 10⁷ m, g = GM/r² = 2.55 N kg⁻¹. (b) Orbital speed v = √(GM/r) = 6.53 × 10³ m s⁻¹. (c) Period T = 2πr/v = 1.61 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses centre-to-centre orbital radius r in g = GM / r².
Applies T = 2πr / v or Kepler's third law.

items.stem: Positioned in a circular orbit of radius 1.71 × 10⁷ m around a spherical terrestrial planet of mass 4.61 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 9.51 × 10⁶ m, a 288 kg synthetic-aperture radar satellite prepares a departure burn (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²). Calculate the local escape speed from r = 1.71 × 10⁷ m.
items.workedSolution: Escape from radial distance r requires ½m v_esc² − GMm/r = 0, so v_esc = √(2GM / r) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 4.61 × 10²⁴ / 1.71 × 10⁷) = 6.00 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

options.distractorRationale: Calculates circular orbital speed √(GM / r) and omits the √2 factor needed to escape from orbit.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates escape speed from the planet's surface R_p rather than from the satellite's orbital radius r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies circular orbital speed by 2 instead of √2.

items.workedSolution: With T = 9200 K and L = 48000 L☉ (note temperature increases from right to left on an HR diagram), Star Theta lies in the supergiant region (supergiant).

items.stem: An unpowered frictionless coaster bogie of mass 46.3 kg enters the bottom of an inverted steel loop-the-loop of radius 9.26 m with horizontal speed 26 m s⁻¹. Resistive forces are negligible; take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 17.7 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 1.11 × 10³ N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 21.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the frictionless coaster bogie as it passes the highest point of the loop.
workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the frictionless coaster bogie at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: Engineers test a 1320 kg urban light-rail maintenance bogie cruising at 11.1 m s⁻¹ on a horizontal depot loop of radius 35 m with μ_s = 0.88 (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the limiting non-skidding speed on this bend.
items.workedSolution: At the verge of skidding, m v_max² / r = μ_s m g, independent of mass: v_max = √(μ_s g r) = √(0.88 × 9.8 × 35) = 17.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates v_max = √(μ_s g r) = 17.4 m s⁻¹.

options.distractorRationale: Divides g r by μ_s instead of multiplying by μ_s under the square root.

options.distractorRationale: Computes μ_s g r and forgets to take the square root when solving m v² / r = μ_s mg.

items.stem: Data from an infrared space observatory for a spherical blackbody cool K-type giant Aldebaran-analog situated 5.09 × 10¹⁶ m from the detector show a spectral peak at λ_max = 400 nm and received radiant flux density 1.289 × 10⁻⁵ W m⁻² (b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K, σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴).
items.workedSolution: (a) Wien's law gives T = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / (400 × 10⁻⁹) = 7.25 × 10³ K. (b) Inverse-square law gives L = 4π d² b_app = 4.20 × 10²⁹ W. (c) Stefan-Boltzmann law gives R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 1.46 × 10¹⁰ m.

markScheme.criterion: Converts nm to m and applies T = b / λ_max.
Rearranges L = 4π R² σ T⁴ for R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the surface temperature of the star.
Show what total luminosity the star radiates by calculating L in watts.
Determine the radius of the star.
workingSteps: From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)].

items.stem: Over a six-month 1 AU baseline, a transit-photometry telescope observes an annual parallax shift of 0.326 arcsec for a solar-type G-dwarf exoplanet host whose luminosity is 3.24 × 10²⁹ W (1 pc is the distance at which a 1 AU baseline subtends a parallax angle of 1 arcsecond, so d / pc = 1 / (p / arcsec)). Use 1 pc = 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 1 / 0.326 = 3.07 pc. (b) In SI units, d = 9.47 × 10¹⁶ m. (c) Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = 2.88 × 10⁻⁶ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies distance in parsecs by 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m pc⁻¹.
Applies inverse-square law b = L / (4π d²).

items.stem: A test mass of 3.6 kg is driven at a constant speed of 4.29 m s⁻¹ around a vertical circle of radius 1.11 m constrained by a circular guide track. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Critical apex speed v_min = √(gR) = 3.30 m s⁻¹. (b) At the top, F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 24.4 N. (c) At the bottom, F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 95.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Sets support force to zero at apex so mg = m v_min² / R.
Subtracts mg from m v² / R at the top.
Adds mg to m v² / R at the bottom.

items.stem: A conical pendulum (0.75 kg, cord length 3.2 m) in an undergraduate mechanics laboratory revolves steadily with its cord inclined at 42 ° to the vertical (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the horizontal acceleration toward the centre of the circle.
items.workedSolution: Dividing horizontal Newton's second law T sin θ = m a_c by vertical equilibrium T cos θ = mg gives a_c = g tan θ = 9.81 × tan 42° = 8.83 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies a_c = g tan 42° to obtain 8.83 m s⁻².

items.stem: Thrusters boost a 1500 kg ocean-altimetry spacecraft around an Earth-mass rocky world (mass 6.14 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.54 × 10⁶ m) from a circular orbit of radius 1.21 × 10⁷ m to a higher circular orbit of radius 4.84 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². What minimum mechanical energy must the thrusters supply?

markScheme.criterion: Uses ΔE_tot = ½GMm(1/r₁ − 1/r₂) to obtain 1.90 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reverses initial and final radii, obtaining a negative energy requirement for raising the orbit.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates |E_tot(r₂)| alone instead of subtracting initial total energy E_tot(r₁) from E_tot(r₂).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the gain in gravitational potential energy ΔE_p = GMm(1/r₁ − 1/r₂) and forgets the virial reduction in kinetic energy (factor of 1/2).

items.stem: Primary (mass 4.18 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Exomoon (mass 4.64 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) have a centre-to-centre separation of 3.35 × 10⁸ m in a sub-Neptune and its massive exomoon. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and zero potential at infinity. What is the combined gravitational potential at the collinear point where the resultant gravitational field is zero?
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 2.51 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -1.48 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -1.48 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Ice Giant of mass 5.36 × 10²⁴ kg (radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Retrograde Moon of mass 6.62 × 10²² kg (radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) form a Neptune–Triton-analog planetary pair separated centre-to-centre by 3.66 × 10⁸ m. Calculate the distance from Ice Giant's centre to the collinear gravitational null point.
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.29 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 3.29 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: Sensors on an iced banked chute corner (radius 45 m, banking 28 °) measure the perpendicular load of a 880 kg bobsleigh cruising with zero side-friction. Using g = 9.81 m s⁻², calculate the normal reaction.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (880 × 9.81) / cos 28° = 9.78 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 28° = mg to obtain N = 9.78 × 10³ N.

items.stem: Photons from the Hydrogen-alpha Balmer transition (λ₀ = 656.3 nm) emitted by a spiral galaxy in the Virgo-analog filament arrive at Earth with wavelength 765.25 nm. Use c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and H₀ = 67.4 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) z = Δλ / λ₀ = 0.166. (b) Scale-factor ratio R / R₀ = 1 / (1 + z) = 0.858. (c) Using v ≈ zc = 4.98 × 10⁴ km s⁻¹, Hubble's law gives d = v / H₀ = 739 Mpc.

markScheme.criterion: Applies z = R₀/R − 1 so R/R₀ = 1 / (1 + z).
Applies v = zc and d = v / H₀.

items.stem: Referenced to zero potential energy at infinity, the orbital energy diagram models a 1390 kg magnetospheric plasma observatory circling a spherical planetary body (mass 3.16 × 10²⁴ kg, surface radius 6.74 × 10⁶ m) at radius r = 1.01 × 10⁷ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k = GMm/(2r) = 1.45 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) E_p = −GMm/r = -2.90 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Total mechanical energy E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = -1.45 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_p = −GMm / r including negative sign.
Sums E_k + E_p or applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of the magnetospheric plasma observatory in this circular orbit.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = G M m / r², E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the magnetospheric plasma observatory.
Determine the total mechanical energy of the magnetospheric plasma observatory.
workingSteps: E_tot = E_k + E_p = −G M m / (2r) = -1.45 × 10¹⁰ J.

items.stem: Compiled during a deep-sky echelle spectrograph programme, an unlabelled Hertzsprung–Russell chart includes Star Delta at effective temperature 4400 K and bolometric luminosity 35000 L☉ (L☉ = 3.83 × 10²⁶ W, R☉ = 6.96 × 10⁸ m, σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴).
items.workedSolution: (a) Star Delta lies in the supergiant region. (b) L = 35000 × 3.83 × 10²⁶ = 1.34 × 10³¹ W. (c) R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 2.24 × 10¹¹ m = 322 R☉.

markScheme.criterion: Applies R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] and divides by R☉.

items.stem: An unpowered 0.5 kg hardened steel ball bearing enters the bottom of a smooth vertical loop track of radius 1.6 m at 10.3 m s⁻¹ under energy-conserving conditions (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What normal contact force acts on it at the apex?
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (10.3)² − 4(9.81)(1.6) = 43.3 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 0.5(43.3 / 1.6 − 9.81) = 8.63 N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 8.63 N.

items.stem: During handling trials on a level compacted-regolith arena, a 1320 kg planetary test rover follows a horizontal circular path of radius 65 m at 19.7 m s⁻¹. Its cleated wheels have a static friction coefficient of 0.82 with the track (g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) a_c = v² / r = (19.7)² / 65 = 5.97 m s⁻². (b) Below the skid limit, f_s = m a_c = 1320 × 5.97 = 7.88 × 10³ N. (c) Maximum non-skidding speed v_max = √(μ_s g r) = 22.9 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies mass by centripetal acceleration (rather than using limiting μ_s mg).
Equates m v_max² / r to μ_s mg.

items.stem: Observations with a high-altitude observatory target a spherical blackbody yellow-white standard-candle star of radius 3.83 × 10⁹ m and effective surface temperature 9600 K situated 2.41 × 10¹⁶ m from the detector. Take σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴. What apparent brightness (radiant intensity) arrives at the detector?
items.workedSolution: Luminosity L = 4π R² σ T⁴ = 4π(3.83 × 10⁹)²(5.67 × 10⁻⁸)(9600)⁴ = 8.88 × 10²⁸ W. Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = σ T⁴ (R / d)² = 1.22 × 10⁻⁵ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses L = 4πR²σT⁴ and b = L / (4πd²) to obtain 1.22 × 10⁻⁵ W m⁻².

items.stem: Astrometric measurements from a stellar intensity interferometer over a 1 AU orbital baseline determine that a bright southern-sky reference star (luminosity 9.96 × 10²⁹ W) has an annual parallax angle of 0.38 arcsec (1 pc is the distance at which a 1 AU baseline subtends a parallax angle of 1 arcsecond, so d / pc = 1 / (p / arcsec)). Take 1 pc = 3.26 ly. What is the distance to the star in light-years?
items.workedSolution: Distance in parsecs d = 1 / p = 1 / 0.38 = 2.63 pc. Converting to light-years gives d = 2.63 × 3.26 = 8.58 ly.

items.stem: Telemetry from a vertical circular stator ring of radius 1.6 m shows a 0.9 kg maglev loop demonstrator sled whirling in a vertical plane at constant speed 6.26 m s⁻¹. Using g = 9.8 m s⁻², determine the normal contact force at the top.
items.workedSolution: At the highest point, both normal contact force and weight mg act downward toward the centre: F_top + mg = m v² / R, so F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 0.9 × ((6.26)² / 1.6 − 9.8) = 13.2 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 13.2 N.

items.stem: Engineers testing rotational instrumentation in a rotational test rig whirl a 2.2 kg capsule on the end of a 1.8 m tether. Throughout the motion, the tether makes a constant semi-vertical angle of 20 ° with the vertical axis. Use g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 20° = (2.2)(9.8) gives T = 22.9 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 1.8 sin 20° = 0.616 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.48 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 2.61 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

items.stem: Around a spherical terrestrial planet (mass 8.53 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 9.0 × 10⁶ m), a 1540 kg synthetic-aperture radar satellite is raised from an inner circular parking orbit of radius r₁ = 1.98 × 10⁷ m to an operational circular orbit of radius r₂ = 7.92 × 10⁷ m. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Initial bound energy E_tot(r₁) = −GMm/(2r₁) = -2.21 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) Final bound energy E_tot(r₂) = -5.53 × 10⁹ J, so ΔE_tot = 1.66 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Outer orbital period T₂ = 2π√(r₂³/GM) = 1.86 × 10⁵ s.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Kepler's third law at outer radius r₂.

items.stem: Mission planners analyse ballistic transfers across a double-planetesimal binary system where Body Alpha (5.83 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) and Body Beta (3.64 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) are separated by 3.95 × 10⁸ m between centres. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and zero potential at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) Null point distance x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.16 × 10⁸ m. (b) Combined scalar potential V(x₀) = -1.54 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. (c) Potential barrier from x = R₁ to x₀ is ΔV = 5.96 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹, giving v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.09 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀).
Equates ½v_min² to potential barrier V(x₀) − V(R₁).

items.stem: Two spherical bodies in an asteroidal binary pair — Primary Asteroid (3.58 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Secondary Moonlet (5.03 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) — lie 7.1 × 10⁸ m apart between centres while a 412 kg ion-beam shepherd craft is located 3.91 × 10⁸ m from Primary Asteroid's centre along their joining line. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 5.16 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 3.91 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.00123 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 0.508 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 0.508 N.

items.stem: Engineers design a banked steel turnaround with a horizontal curve radius of 120 m and banking angle 28 ° so that a 1950 kg train corners in a horizontal plane with zero sideways friction (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 28° = mg gives N = 2.17 × 10⁴ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 28° = 1.02 × 10⁴ N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 25.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the train.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 25.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In an extragalactic survey with H₀ = 72 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, the neutral Helium spectral line (rest wavelength 587.6 nm) from an isolated ring galaxy arrives at 598.18 nm. Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the Hubble distance in Mpc.
items.workedSolution: Redshift z = (λ_obs − λ₀) / λ₀ = (598.18 − 587.6) / 587.6 = 0.0180. Recession speed v ≈ z c = 5.40 × 10³ km s⁻¹. From Hubble's law v = H₀ d, d = v / H₀ = 5.40 × 10³ / 72 = 75.0 Mpc.

markScheme.criterion: Finds z = 0.0180, v = 5.40 × 10³ km s⁻¹, and d = v / H₀ = 75.0 Mpc.

items.stem: Orbital telemetry tracks a 226 kg cryogenic infrared space telescope maintaining circular motion at height h = 1.84 × 10⁶ m above a terrestrial host planet of mass 3.68 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 5.25 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) With orbital radius r = 7.09 × 10⁶ m, g = GM/r² = 4.88 N kg⁻¹. (b) Orbital speed v = √(GM/r) = 5.88 × 10³ m s⁻¹. (c) Period T = 2πr/v = 7.57 × 10³ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses centre-to-centre orbital radius r in g = GM / r².
Applies T = 2πr / v or Kepler's third law.

items.stem: Determine the escape velocity from orbital radius r = 1.77 × 10⁷ m for a 1100 kg laser-interferometry geodesy orbiter orbiting a spherical silicate planet of mass 1.49 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 4.92 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Escape from radial distance r requires ½m v_esc² − GMm/r = 0, so v_esc = √(2GM / r) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 1.49 × 10²⁵ / 1.77 × 10⁷) = 1.06 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates circular orbital speed √(GM / r) and omits the √2 factor needed to escape from orbit.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies circular orbital speed by 2 instead of √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates escape speed from the planet's surface R_p rather than from the satellite's orbital radius r.

items.stem: Photometry in an orbital observatory HR calibration field locates Star Kappa at effective temperature 3600 K and luminosity 320 L☉ on the Hertzsprung–Russell chart. Taking L☉ = 3.83 × 10²⁶ W, R☉ = 6.96 × 10⁸ m, and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, find its radius in R☉.
items.workedSolution: Luminosity L = 320 × 3.83 × 10²⁶ = 1.23 × 10²⁹ W. From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] = 3.20 × 10¹⁰ m, so R / R☉ = R / (6.96 × 10⁸) = 46.0 R☉.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Stefan-Boltzmann scaling to obtain 46.0 R☉.

items.stem: An unpowered skatepark test trolley of mass 1.8 kg enters the bottom of a smooth circular vertical cradle of radius 4.2 m with horizontal speed 20.7 m s⁻¹. Resistive forces are negligible; take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 16.2 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 95.3 N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 14.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the skatepark test trolley as it passes the highest point of the loop.
workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the skatepark test trolley at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: What minimum static friction coefficient allows a 1150 kg planetary test rover to negotiate a level compacted-regolith arena of radius 28 m at 11.7 m s⁻¹ without skidding? Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: No-skid cornering requires μ_s m g ≥ m v² / r, so μ_min = v² / (g r) = (11.7)² / (9.8 × 28) = 0.499.

items.stem: Using a 1 AU orbital baseline, a wide-field photometric survey measures an annual parallax angle of 0.68 arcsec for a metal-poor halo giant star of total luminosity 6.89 × 10²⁹ W (1 pc is the distance at which a 1 AU baseline subtends a parallax angle of 1 arcsecond, so d / pc = 1 / (p / arcsec)). Take 1 pc = 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 1 / 0.68 = 1.47 pc. (b) In SI units, d = 4.54 × 10¹⁶ m. (c) Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = 2.66 × 10⁻⁵ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies distance in parsecs by 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m pc⁻¹.
Applies inverse-square law b = L / (4π d²).

items.stem: Motorized drive control keeps a 0.794 kg mass moving at constant tangential speed 7.65 m s⁻¹ around a vertical circular path of radius 2.33 m using an inextensible tether. Use g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Critical apex speed v_min = √(gR) = 4.78 m s⁻¹. (b) At the top, F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 12.2 N. (c) At the bottom, F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 27.7 N.

markScheme.criterion: Sets support force to zero at apex so mg = m v_min² / R.
Subtracts mg from m v² / R at the top.
Adds mg to m v² / R at the bottom.

items.stem: A 1.2 kg wind-tunnel tethered aerodynamic probe attached to a 1.65 m light wire revolves in a horizontal circle inside a rotary calibration fixture at a constant semi-vertical angle of 24 °. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the time period of one complete revolution?
items.workedSolution: From T cos θ = mg and T sin θ = m ω² (L sin θ), ω = √(g / (L cos θ)). Thus the period is P = 2π√(L cos θ / g) = 2π√((1.65 cos 24°) / 9.8) = 2.46 s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates 2π√(L cos 24° / g) to obtain 2.46 s.

items.stem: Comparing circular orbits of radii r₁ = 1.78 × 10⁷ m and r₂ = 6.41 × 10⁷ m around a spherical planetary body (mass 6.49 × 10²⁴ kg, surface radius 7.11 × 10⁶ m), find the signed change in orbital kinetic energy for a 1270 kg magnetospheric plasma observatory raised from r₁ to r₂ (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Because E_k(r) = +GMm/(2r) decreases as r increases, ΔE_k = ½GMm(1/r₂ − 1/r₁) = -1.12 × 10¹⁰ J.

items.stem: Determine the least initial speed at Primary Asteroid's surface (1.32 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.37 × 10⁶ m) enabling a ballistic ion-beam shepherd craft to reach Secondary Moonlet (8.25 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) across a 6.05 × 10⁸ m centre-to-centre baseline (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Surface potential at x = R₁ is V(R₁) = −GM₁/R₁ − GM₂/(d − R₁) = -1.38 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹. Null-point potential at x₀ = 4.84 × 10⁸ m is V(x₀) = -2.27 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. Potential barrier ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 1.36 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹, so v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.65 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) and v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.65 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Inside a uniform-density tidally locked silicate exoplanet of total mass 2.77 × 10²⁵ kg and surface radius 7.76 × 10⁶ m, a 190 kg descent lander takes gravimetric readings at r = 4.27 × 10⁶ m from the centre. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Surface field g₀ = GM/R² = 30.7 N kg⁻¹. (b) At r = 4.27 × 10⁶ m, uniform-sphere interior scaling g = g₀(r/R) gives 16.9 N kg⁻¹. (c) Force on probe F = mg = 3.21 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes M and R into g₀ = GM / R².
Applies linear interior field law g(r) = GMr/R³.
Multiplies probe mass by field strength at r.

items.stem: Along the line joining World P (mass 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and World Q (mass 9.55 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m) separated centre-to-centre by 4.03 × 10⁸ m, a 900 kg ballistic research capsule is at distance 2.22 × 10⁸ m from World P's centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². What is the magnitude of the resultant gravitational field due to both bodies at the ballistic research capsule?
items.workedSolution: Between the two centres, the gravitational fields oppose: |g_net| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = |0.00808 − 0.00194| = 0.00614 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field magnitudes to obtain 0.00614 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Rounding a superelevated guideway curve (radius 145 m, bank angle 28 °) with zero lateral friction, a 640 kg carriage stays in a horizontal circle. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², determine the normal reaction force.
items.workedSolution: Because the circular path lies in a horizontal plane, vertical acceleration is zero: N cos θ = mg, so N = (640 × 9.81) / cos 28° = 7.11 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves vertically N cos 28° = mg to obtain N = 7.11 × 10³ N.

items.stem: A elliptical cluster galaxy is observed spectroscopically. The singly ionized Calcium K absorption line, which has rest wavelength 393.4 nm in the laboratory, appears at observed wavelength 400.76 nm. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and H₀ = 73.5 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) z = (λ_obs − λ₀)/λ₀ = 0.0187. (b) Recession speed v ≈ zc = 5.61 × 10³ km s⁻¹. (c) Hubble distance d = v/H₀ = 76.4 Mpc.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies z by c and converts to km s⁻¹.

items.stem: Referenced to zero potential energy at infinity, the orbital energy diagram models a 432 kg autonomous orbital servicing tug circling a dense terrestrial world (mass 8.6 × 10²⁴ kg, surface radius 6.55 × 10⁶ m) at radius r = 1.44 × 10⁷ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k = GMm/(2r) = 8.60 × 10⁹ J. (b) E_p = −GMm/r = -1.72 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Total mechanical energy E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = -8.60 × 10⁹ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_p = −GMm / r including negative sign.
Sums E_k + E_p or applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of the autonomous orbital servicing tug in this circular orbit.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = G M m / r², E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the autonomous orbital servicing tug.
Determine the total mechanical energy of the autonomous orbital servicing tug.
workingSteps: E_tot = E_k + E_p = −G M m / (2r) = -8.60 × 10⁹ J.

items.stem: The Hertzsprung–Russell diagram from a southern-hemisphere spectroscopic star survey plots four stars with region names masked. Star Beta has surface temperature 15000 K and luminosity 0.004 L☉. Take L☉ = 3.83 × 10²⁶ W, R☉ = 6.96 × 10⁸ m, and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) Star Beta lies in the white-dwarf region. (b) L = 0.004 × 3.83 × 10²⁶ = 1.53 × 10²⁴ W. (c) R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 6.52 × 10⁶ m = 0.00936 R☉.

markScheme.criterion: Applies R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] and divides by R☉.

items.stem: In a test run on a full vertical circular arc of radius 0.635 m, a 0.212 kg pendulum impact bob enters the bottom at 8.48 m s⁻¹ with negligible friction (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the minimum bottom entry speed that would still allow it to complete the full vertical loop without losing contact at the top?
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.8 × 0.635) = 5.58 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: An autonomous delivery pod of mass 1650 kg travels at a constant speed of 13 m s⁻¹ along a level campus courtyard curve of radius 52 m. The coefficient of static friction between its pneumatic tyres and the ground is 0.68. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) a_c = v² / r = (13)² / 52 = 3.25 m s⁻². (b) Below the skid limit, f_s = m a_c = 1650 × 3.25 = 5.36 × 10³ N. (c) Maximum non-skidding speed v_max = √(μ_s g r) = 18.6 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies mass by centripetal acceleration (rather than using limiting μ_s mg).
Equates m v_max² / r to μ_s mg.
