items.stem: The blackbody continuum of a nearby M-dwarf flare star (radius 1.55 × 10¹⁰ m, distance 1.56 × 10¹⁶ m) corresponds to an effective photospheric temperature of 14800 K as recorded by a cooled CCD radiometer. Take Wien's constant b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K. At what wavelength, in nm, does its emitted spectrum peak?
items.workedSolution: Using Wien's displacement law, λ_max = b / T = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / 14800 = 1.96 × 10⁻⁷ m = 196 nm.

items.stem: Calculate the road normal reaction on a 1350 kg vintage touring car cresting the circular crest of a humpback stone bridge of radius 44 m at constant speed 17.9 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At the convex crest, downward resultant force is mg − N_top = m v² / R, so N_top = m(g − v²/R) = 1350 × (9.81 − (17.9)² / 44) = 3.41 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 3.41 × 10³ N.

items.stem: In a steam-turbine speed regulator, a centrifugal flyball governor mass of mass 0.75 kg is suspended from a fixed ceiling pivot by a light inextensible cord of length 0.95 m. The governor mass moves at constant speed in a horizontal circle such that the cord maintains a steady angle of 24 ° to the vertical. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium T cos 24° = (0.75)(9.8) gives T = 8.05 N. (b) Horizontal radius r = 0.95 sin 24° = 0.386 m; horizontal dynamics T sin θ = mv²/r yields v = 1.30 m s⁻¹. (c) Period P = 2πr / v = 1.87 s.

markScheme.criterion: Equates vertical component T cos θ to weight mg.
Uses r = L sin θ and equates T sin θ (or mg tan θ) to m v² / r.
Applies P = 2π r / v or P = 2π√(L cos θ / g).

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the cord supporting the governor mass.
workingSteps: Vertical force balance gives T cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the linear speed of the governor mass along its horizontal circular path.
workingSteps: Horizontal radius r = L sin θ = 0.95 sin 24° = 0.386 m.
From T sin θ = m v² / r, v = √(g r tan θ) = 1.30 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the time period for one complete revolution of the governor mass.

items.stem: Around a rocky central planet (mass 1.07 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m), a 600 kg ion-propelled communications relay is raised from an inner circular parking orbit of radius r₁ = 1.39 × 10⁷ m to an operational circular orbit of radius r₂ = 3.34 × 10⁷ m. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Initial bound energy E_tot(r₁) = −GMm/(2r₁) = -1.54 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) Final bound energy E_tot(r₂) = -6.41 × 10⁹ J, so ΔE_tot = 8.99 × 10⁹ J. (c) Outer orbital period T₂ = 2π√(r₂³/GM) = 4.54 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Kepler's third law at outer radius r₂.

parts.prompt: Calculate the initial total mechanical energy of the ion-propelled communications relay in the orbit of radius r₁.
Determine the minimum mechanical energy that must be supplied to transfer the ion-propelled communications relay into the circular orbit of radius r₂.
Calculate the orbital period of the ion-propelled communications relay in the outer circular orbit of radius r₂.

items.stem: Two non-rotating airless spherical bodies in a Neptune–Triton-analog planetary pair — Ice Giant of mass 1.64 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m, and Retrograde Moon of mass 6.56 × 10²³ kg and radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m — have a centre-to-centre separation of 3.0 × 10⁸ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and potential to be zero at infinity.
items.workedSolution: (a) Null point distance x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 2.50 × 10⁸ m. (b) Combined scalar potential V(x₀) = -5.25 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. (c) Potential barrier from x = R₁ to x₀ is ΔV = 1.44 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹, giving v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.70 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀).
Equates ½v_min² to potential barrier V(x₀) − V(R₁).

workingSteps: Equating field magnitudes gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 2.50 × 10⁸ m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the combined gravitational potential at this null point.
workingSteps: V(x₀) = −G M₁ / x₀ − G M₂ / (d − x₀) = -5.25 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Determine the minimum launch speed from the surface of Ice Giant along the line of centres required for a deep-space relay probe to reach Retrograde Moon.
workingSteps: ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 1.44 × 10⁸ J kg⁻¹; v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.70 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A radial drill shaft inside a uniform spherical basaltic terrestrial planetoid (total mass 2.69 × 10²⁵ kg, surface radius 4.92 × 10⁶ m) stations a 123 kg orbital transponder at r = 3.2 × 10⁶ m from the centre. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², determine g(r).
items.workedSolution: Inside a uniform sphere (r < R), enclosed mass M_enc = M(r/R)³, so g(r) = G M r / R³ = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.69 × 10²⁵ × 3.2 × 10⁶) / (4.92 × 10⁶)³ = 48.2 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates gravitational field strength at r = 3.2 × 10⁶ m to obtain 48.2 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: A spherical charted extrasolar rocky world (mass 8.95 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 8.28 × 10⁶ m) is observed by a 620 kg magnetospheric probe at radial distance 2.65 × 10⁷ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², at what minimum speed must an object leave the surface R to reach infinity?
items.workedSolution: Setting ½m v_esc² − G M m / R = 0 gives v_esc = √(2 G M / R) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 8.95 × 10²⁴ / 8.28 × 10⁶) = 1.20 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates surface escape speed √(2GM / R) = 1.20 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Two spherical bodies in a double-planetesimal binary system — Body Alpha (6.14 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Body Beta (6.82 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m) — lie 3.56 × 10⁸ m apart between centres while a 926 kg sample-return lander is located 1.25 × 10⁸ m from Body Alpha's centre along their joining line. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Equating GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)² yields x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 2.67 × 10⁸ m. (b) At x = 1.25 × 10⁸ m, |g| = |GM₁/x² − GM₂/(d − x)²| = 0.0254 N kg⁻¹. (c) Net force F = m|g| = 23.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Equates opposing inverse-square field strengths GM₁/x₀² = GM₂/(d − x₀)².
Takes square root correctly to form x₀ = d√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂).
Subtracts opposing field magnitudes at x and (d − x).
Multiplies by spacecraft mass to obtain 23.5 N.

workingSteps: At the null point, G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)².
Taking square roots gives x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 2.67 × 10⁸ m.

workingSteps: |g| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = 0.0254 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: An autonomous mining haul truck of combined mass 1050 kg travels around a banked quarry spiral ramp of horizontal radius 58 m inclined at a constant banking angle of 16 ° to the horizontal. At the chosen design speed, zero lateral frictional force acts along the slope. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical equilibrium N cos 16° = mg gives N = 1.07 × 10⁴ N. (b) Horizontal component F_c = N sin 16° = 2.95 × 10³ N. (c) Setting m v² / r = F_c yields v_ideal = 12.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N cos θ = mg (zero vertical acceleration).
Evaluates F_c = N sin θ or mg tan θ.
Equates m v² / r to F_c and solves for v.

parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the truck.
workingSteps: Vertical equilibrium gives N cos θ = mg.

parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal centripetal force acting toward the centre of curvature.
workingSteps: Horizontal component of normal reaction provides the centripetal force: F_c = N sin θ = mg tan θ.

parts.prompt: Hence calculate the ideal frictionless cornering speed of the truck.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = F_c, v = √(F_c r / m) = √(g r tan θ) = 12.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In the spectrum of a star-forming barred spiral galaxy (surveyed with H₀ = 67.4 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹), the Hydrogen-beta Balmer emission line of rest wavelength 486.1 nm is measured at 494.85 nm. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What is the recession speed of the galaxy in km s⁻¹?
items.workedSolution: z = Δλ / λ₀ = (494.85 − 486.1) / 486.1 = 0.0180. In the low-redshift regime, v ≈ z c = 0.0180 × 3.00 × 10⁵ km s⁻¹ = 5.40 × 10³ km s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v ≈ (Δλ / λ₀) c to obtain 5.40 × 10³ km s⁻¹.

items.stem: An autonomous orbital servicing tug of mass 638 kg moves in a circular orbit of radius 1.583 × 10⁷ m around a dense terrestrial world of mass 7.99 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 7.54 × 10⁶ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) With orbital radius r = 1.583 × 10⁷ m, g = GM/r² = 2.13 N kg⁻¹. (b) Orbital speed v = √(GM/r) = 5.80 × 10³ m s⁻¹. (c) Period T = 2πr/v = 1.71 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses centre-to-centre orbital radius r in g = GM / r².
Applies T = 2πr / v or Kepler's third law.

items.stem: Orbiting a terrestrial host planet (mass 2.99 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 4.78 × 10⁶ m) at circular orbital radius 7.17 × 10⁶ m, a 280 kg cryogenic infrared space telescope is gravitationally bound. With E_p = 0 at infinity and G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate its total mechanical energy.
items.workedSolution: In a circular orbit, E_k = +GMm/(2r) and E_p = −GMm/r, so E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.99 × 10²⁴ × 280) / (2 × 7.17 × 10⁶) = -3.89 × 10⁹ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r) with negative sign to obtain -3.89 × 10⁹ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_tot = −GMm/(2r), quoting gravitational potential energy −GMm/r instead.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the negative bound-state sign, reporting +GMm/(2r) instead of −GMm/(2r).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits both the negative sign and the virial factor of 1/2, reporting +GMm/r.

items.stem: In a globular-cluster stellar population chart, Star Iota is plotted on the Hertzsprung–Russell diagram at surface temperature 7600 K and luminosity 14 L☉. Take L☉ = 3.83 × 10²⁶ W, R☉ = 6.96 × 10⁸ m, and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴. What is the radius of Star Iota in solar radii (R☉)?
items.workedSolution: Luminosity L = 14 × 3.83 × 10²⁶ = 5.36 × 10²⁷ W. From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] = 1.50 × 10⁹ m, so R / R☉ = R / (6.96 × 10⁸) = 2.16 R☉.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Stefan-Boltzmann scaling to obtain 2.16 R☉.

items.stem: In a vertical-loop mechanics experiment, a 360 kg frictionless coaster bogie is launched horizontally at 10.3 m s⁻¹ into the base of an inverted steel loop-the-loop of radius 1.6 m where friction is negligible (g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Using ½mv_bot² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R), v_top = √(v_bot² − 4gR) = 6.59 m s⁻¹. (b) Downward radial balance F_top + mg = mv_top²/R gives F_top = 6.23 × 10³ N. (c) Setting F_top = 0 gives v_top = √(gR) and v_bot,min = √(5gR) = 8.85 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies energy conservation with vertical rise Δh = 2R.
Uses F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) at the apex.
Combines v_top,min² = gR with v_bot,min² = v_top,min² + 4gR.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the frictionless coaster bogie as it passes the highest point of the loop.
workingSteps: Conservation of mechanical energy with Δh = 2R gives v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR.

parts.prompt: Determine the magnitude of the normal contact force acting on the frictionless coaster bogie at the highest point.
workingSteps: At the apex, F_top + mg = m v_top² / R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the minimum speed at the bottom of the loop required to complete the circle without losing contact at the top.
workingSteps: At threshold contact, v_top = √(gR), so v_bot,min = √(gR + 4gR) = √(5gR).

items.stem: A 920 kg track-cycling sprinter circles the flat warm-up apron inside a velodrome of radius 44 m at 11.8 m s⁻¹. If μ_s = 0.48 and g = 9.81 m s⁻², what critical speed marks the onset of skidding?
items.workedSolution: At the verge of skidding, m v_max² / r = μ_s m g, independent of mass: v_max = √(μ_s g r) = √(0.48 × 9.81 × 44) = 14.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates v_max = √(μ_s g r) = 14.4 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Astrometry from a calibrated bolometric detector across Earth's 1 AU orbital radius records parallax p = 0.26 arcsec for a young open-cluster A-type star radiating bolometric luminosity 9.96 × 10²⁸ W (1 pc is the distance at which a 1 AU baseline subtends a parallax angle of 1 arcsecond, so d / pc = 1 / (p / arcsec)) (1 pc = 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m).
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 1 / 0.26 = 3.85 pc. (b) In SI units, d = 1.19 × 10¹⁷ m. (c) Apparent brightness b = L / (4π d²) = 5.63 × 10⁻⁷ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies distance in parsecs by 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m pc⁻¹.
Applies inverse-square law b = L / (4π d²).

items.stem: As shown in the vertical-plane diagram, an inextensible tether constrains a 1.29 kg mass to revolve uniformly at 7.69 m s⁻¹ on a circle of radius 2.68 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Critical apex speed v_min = √(gR) = 5.13 m s⁻¹. (b) At the top, F_top = m(v²/R − g) = 15.8 N. (c) At the bottom, F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 41.1 N.

markScheme.criterion: Sets support force to zero at apex so mg = m v_min² / R.
Subtracts mg from m v² / R at the top.
Adds mg to m v² / R at the bottom.

items.stem: In a vibration-isolated calibration bay, a ceiling-mounted metrology plummet of mass 0.35 kg hangs from an inextensible cord of length 0.8 m and sweeps a horizontal circle at a constant semi-vertical angle of 24 °. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the tension in the cord?
items.workedSolution: Vertical equilibrium requires T cos θ = mg, so T = (0.35 × 9.8) / cos 24° = 3.75 N.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves T cos 24° = mg to obtain T = 3.75 N.

items.stem: A 1590 kg planetary gravity-mapping orbiter around a uniform spherical planet (mass 8.76 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 6.19 × 10⁶ m) executes an elliptical Hohmann transfer with periapsis r₁ = 8.67 × 10⁶ m and apoapsis r₂ = 3.47 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². How long does the half-ellipse coast from r₁ to r₂ take?
items.workedSolution: The transfer ellipse has semi-major axis a = ½(r₁ + r₂) = 2.17 × 10⁷ m. Coasting from periapsis to apoapsis takes half an orbital period: t_H = π√(a³ / GM) = 1.31 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses a = ½(r₁ + r₂) and t_H = π√(a³ / GM) to obtain 1.31 × 10⁴ s.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Averages the inner and outer half-periods linearly rather than applying T ∝ a^(3/2).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the full elliptical period 2π√(a³ / GM) instead of the half-orbit Hohmann coast time π√(a³ / GM).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses major axis (r₁ + r₂) instead of semi-major axis a = (r₁ + r₂)/2 in Kepler's third law.

items.stem: Along the 3.84 × 10⁸ m line of centres of a terrestrial bi-planetary system, Planet Major (6.87 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Planet Minor (2.75 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) create a zero-field saddle point. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², find the total gravitational potential there.
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.20 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -1.72 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -1.72 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

items.workedSolution: (a) Surface field g₀ = GM/R² = 24.7 N kg⁻¹. (b) At r = 4.43 × 10⁶ m, uniform-sphere interior scaling g = g₀(r/R) gives 18.6 N kg⁻¹. (c) Force on probe F = mg = 1.57 × 10⁴ N.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes M and R into g₀ = GM / R².

Multiplies probe mass by field strength at r.

items.stem: Mission analysts model a non-rotating airless synthetic uniform planetary body of mass 2.85 × 10²⁴ kg and surface radius 1.22 × 10⁷ m, together with a 656 kg deep-shaft gravimeter at distance 3.9 × 10⁷ m from its centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) V_surface = −GM/R = -1.56 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹. (b) Escape speed v_esc = √(−2 V_surface) = √(2GM/R) = 5.58 × 10³ m s⁻¹. (c) At r = 3.9 × 10⁷ m, E_p = −GMm/r = -3.20 × 10⁹ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_g = −GM / R with negative sign.
Applies E_p = −GMm / r at probe radius.

items.stem: Between Primary Planet (mass 1.39 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 7.33 × 10⁶ m) and Companion Moon (mass 3.86 × 10²³ kg, radius 2.09 × 10⁶ m), whose centres are 7.51 × 10⁸ m apart, find the combined gravitational field strength at a 978 kg cislunar transfer probe located 2.63 × 10⁸ m from Primary Planet's centre (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Between the two centres, the gravitational fields oppose: |g_net| = |G M₁ / x² − G M₂ / (d − x)²| = |0.0134 − 1.08 × 10⁻⁴| = 0.0133 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts opposing inverse-square field magnitudes to obtain 0.0133 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: Without relying on lateral tyre or rail grip, a 1050 kg autonomous mining haul truck negotiates a banked quarry spiral ramp of radius 105 m inclined at 14 ° to the horizontal (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find its speed.
items.workedSolution: With zero slope friction, N cos θ = mg and N sin θ = m v² / r. Dividing gives tan θ = v² / (g r), so v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.8 × 105 × tan 14°) = 16.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = √(g r tan 14°) to obtain 16.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Mission tracking places a 750 kg ultraviolet spectroscopy satellite at height 7.65 × 10⁶ m above an airless rocky planet of mass 1.01 × 10²⁵ kg and radius 5.1 × 10⁶ m (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²). Calculate the orbital period.
items.workedSolution: Orbital radius from planet centre r = R_p + h = 5.1 × 10⁶ + 7.65 × 10⁶ = 1.275 × 10⁷ m. By Kepler's third law, T = 2π√(r³ / GM) = 2π√((1.275 × 10⁷)³ / (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 1.01 × 10²⁵)) = 1.10 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = 1.275 × 10⁷ m to obtain 1.10 × 10⁴ s.

items.stem: In a circular orbit of centre-to-centre radius 2.18 × 10⁷ m around a terrestrial host planet (mass 1.53 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.06 × 10⁶ m), a 906 kg cryogenic infrared space telescope has E_p = 0 at infinity. Use G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k = GMm/(2r) = 2.12 × 10¹⁰ J. (b) E_p = −GMm/r = -4.24 × 10¹⁰ J. (c) Total mechanical energy E_tot = E_k + E_p = −GMm/(2r) = -2.12 × 10¹⁰ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_p = −GMm / r including negative sign.
Sums E_k + E_p or applies E_tot = −GMm / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of the cryogenic infrared space telescope in this circular orbit.
workingSteps: From m v² / r = G M m / r², E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r).

parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of the cryogenic infrared space telescope.
Determine the total mechanical energy of the cryogenic infrared space telescope.
workingSteps: E_tot = E_k + E_p = −G M m / (2r) = -2.12 × 10¹⁰ J.

items.stem: The Hertzsprung–Russell diagram from a southern-hemisphere spectroscopic star survey plots four stars with region names masked. Star Mu has surface temperature 5400 K and luminosity 22000 L☉. Take L☉ = 3.83 × 10²⁶ W, R☉ = 6.96 × 10⁸ m, and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) Star Mu lies in the supergiant region. (b) L = 22000 × 3.83 × 10²⁶ = 8.43 × 10³⁰ W. (c) R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 1.18 × 10¹¹ m = 169 R☉.

markScheme.criterion: Applies R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] and divides by R☉.

items.stem: An unpowered 0.5 kg hardened steel ball bearing enters the bottom of a smooth vertical loop track of radius 1.2 m at 8.9 m s⁻¹ under energy-conserving conditions (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What normal contact force acts on it at the apex?
items.workedSolution: At the top, v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR = (8.9)² − 4(9.81)(1.2) = 32.1 m² s⁻². Radial force balance F_top + mg = m v_top² / R gives F_top = 0.5(32.1 / 1.2 − 9.81) = 8.48 N.

markScheme.criterion: Combines v_top² = v_bot² − 4gR with F_top = m(v_top²/R − g) to obtain 8.48 N.

items.stem: Engineers test a 1650 kg urban light-rail maintenance bogie cruising at 16.4 m s⁻¹ on a horizontal depot loop of radius 90 m with μ_s = 0.74 (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the limiting non-skidding speed on this bend.
items.workedSolution: At the verge of skidding, m v_max² / r = μ_s m g, independent of mass: v_max = √(μ_s g r) = √(0.74 × 9.8 × 90) = 25.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates v_max = √(μ_s g r) = 25.5 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Observations by a stellar intensity interferometer yield bolometric luminosity L = 2.059 × 10³⁰ W and Wien peak wavelength 195.9 nm for a spherical blackbody bright southern-sky reference star. Taking b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, find R.
items.workedSolution: By Wien's law, T = b / λ_max = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / (195.9 × 10⁻⁹) = 1.48 × 10⁴ K. From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] = 7.76 × 10⁹ m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds T = 1.48 × 10⁴ K via Wien's law and R = √[L/(4πσT⁴)] = 7.76 × 10⁹ m.

items.stem: Determine the apparent brightness b = L / (4πd²) at Earth for a luminous F-type subgiant of luminosity 4.74 × 10²⁸ W whose 1 AU astrometric parallax in a space-based spectrometer is 0.127 arcsec (1 pc is the distance at which a 1 AU baseline subtends a parallax angle of 1 arcsecond, so d / pc = 1 / (p / arcsec)) (1 pc = 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m).

markScheme.criterion: Converts d = (1/p) pc to metres and evaluates b = L/(4πd²) = 6.39 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻².

items.stem: Passing through the bottom of a vertical circular trajectory of radius 0.85 m at steady speed 3.87 m s⁻¹, a 1.6 kg maglev loop demonstrator sled is constrained by a vertical circular stator ring (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the upward normal contact force.
items.workedSolution: At the lowest point, upward normal contact force opposes downward weight mg to produce upward centripetal acceleration: F_bot − mg = m v² / R, giving F_bot = m(v²/R + g) = 1.6 × ((3.87)² / 0.85 + 9.8) = 43.9 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses F_bot = m(v²/R + g) to obtain 43.9 N.

items.stem: A 2.4 m tether in a steady slewing test guides a 0.85 kg ballast block around a horizontal circle at a steady cone half-angle of 42 ° (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Find the inward radial acceleration of the ballast block.
items.workedSolution: Dividing horizontal Newton's second law T sin θ = m a_c by vertical equilibrium T cos θ = mg gives a_c = g tan θ = 9.81 × tan 42° = 8.83 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies a_c = g tan 42° to obtain 8.83 m s⁻².

items.stem: Upon moving from a lower circular orbit of radius 1.32 × 10⁷ m to an outer circular orbit of radius 2.64 × 10⁷ m about a spherical terrestrial planet (mass 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 8.28 × 10⁶ m), calculate the signed kinetic energy change ΔE_k of a 450 kg synthetic-aperture radar satellite (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Because E_k(r) = +GMm/(2r) decreases as r increases, ΔE_k = ½GMm(1/r₂ − 1/r₁) = -3.39 × 10⁹ J.

items.stem: From the airless surface of Primary Planet (mass 7.27 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m), a cislunar transfer probe is fired along the line of centres toward Companion Moon (mass 2.02 × 10²³ kg, radius 1.83 × 10⁶ m) at separation 2.92 × 10⁸ m. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², determine the threshold launch speed to cross the null-point barrier.
items.workedSolution: Surface potential at x = R₁ is V(R₁) = −GM₁/R₁ − GM₂/(d − R₁) = -8.97 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹. Null-point potential at x₀ = 2.50 × 10⁸ m is V(x₀) = -2.26 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹. Potential barrier ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) = 8.74 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹, so v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.32 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔV = V(x₀) − V(R₁) and v_min = √(2ΔV) = 1.32 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Model a charted extrasolar rocky world as a sphere of uniform density with total mass 4.92 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 4.92 × 10⁶ m. A magnetospheric probe of mass 370 kg descends along a radial borehole to distance 1.97 × 10⁶ m from the planet's centre. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². What is the gravitational field strength at this interior point?
items.workedSolution: Inside a uniform sphere (r < R), enclosed mass M_enc = M(r/R)³, so g(r) = G M r / R³ = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 4.92 × 10²⁴ × 1.97 × 10⁶) / (4.92 × 10⁶)³ = 5.43 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates gravitational field strength at r = 1.97 × 10⁶ m to obtain 5.43 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: A spherical basaltic terrestrial planetoid (mass 4.42 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.72 × 10⁶ m) is observed by a 825 kg orbital transponder at radial distance 2.17 × 10⁷ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², at what minimum speed must an object leave the surface R to reach infinity?
items.workedSolution: Setting ½m v_esc² − G M m / R = 0 gives v_esc = √(2 G M / R) = √(2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 4.42 × 10²⁴ / 5.72 × 10⁶) = 1.02 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates surface escape speed √(2GM / R) = 1.02 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Ice Giant of mass 6.32 × 10²⁴ kg (radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Retrograde Moon of mass 7.8 × 10²² kg (radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) form a Neptune–Triton-analog planetary pair separated centre-to-centre by 3.66 × 10⁸ m. Calculate the distance from Ice Giant's centre to the collinear gravitational null point.
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 3.29 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 3.29 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: On a canted main-line viaduct curve (radius 105 m, bank angle 28 °, μ_s = 0.25), a 1050 kg coach currently travels at 26.9 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², calculate the upper non-skidding speed limit.
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 28° + 0.25 cos 28°) / (cos 28° − 0.25 sin 28°)] = 30.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 30.5 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the ratio R / R₀ of the cosmic scale factor at emission to its value today for a elliptical cluster galaxy whose singly ionized Calcium K absorption line shifts from 393.4 nm to 491.75 nm (H₀ = 70 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: Since 1 + z = R₀ / R = λ_obs / λ₀, the emission-to-present scale-factor ratio is R / R₀ = λ₀ / λ_obs = 393.4 / 491.75 = 0.800.

items.stem: Orbiting a rocky central planet (mass 4.61 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.9 × 10⁶ m) along a circle of radius 8.85 × 10⁶ m, an ion-propelled communications relay has mass 1650 kg. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², calculate the orbital kinetic energy of the spacecraft.
items.workedSolution: Since m v² / r = G M m / r², orbital kinetic energy is E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r) = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 4.61 × 10²⁴ × 1650) / (2 × 8.85 × 10⁶) = 2.87 × 10¹⁰ J.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_k = ½mv² = GMm/(2r), computing GMm/r instead.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses surface altitude (r − R_p) instead of orbital radius r.

items.stem: A 0.8 kg low-friction maglev test sled currently enters a vertical circular guide ring of radius 6.5 m at 21.8 m s⁻¹ under frictionless conditions (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the critical minimum speed at the bottom required to just clear the apex.
items.workedSolution: Maintaining contact at the apex requires v_top ≥ √(gR). Conservation of energy from bottom to top (Δh = 2R) gives ½m v_bot,min² = ½m(gR) + mg(2R) => v_bot,min = √(5gR) = √(5 × 9.8 × 6.5) = 17.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Telemetry from a 1650 kg short-track speed-skating sled cornering without slip on a flat synthetic training ring (radius 105 m, μ_s = 0.36) records a speed of 14.6 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², find the static frictional force exerted by the ground.
items.workedSolution: Because 14.6 m s⁻¹ is below the skidding threshold v_max = √(μ_s g r) = 19.2 m s⁻¹, static friction self-adjusts to match the required centripetal force: f_s = m v² / r = 1650 × (14.6)² / 105 = 3.35 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses f_s = m v² / r (not μ_s mg) to obtain 3.35 × 10³ N.

items.workedSolution: Using Wien's displacement law, λ_max = b / T = 2.90 × 10⁻³ / 9820 = 2.95 × 10⁻⁷ m = 295 nm.

items.stem: Determine the annual parallax angle (in arcsec, 1 AU baseline) of a evolved red-clump giant whose luminosity is 1.51 × 10²⁹ W and whose apparent brightness recorded by an astrometric space mission is 2.954 × 10⁻⁷ W m⁻² (1 pc is the distance at which a 1 AU baseline subtends a parallax angle of 1 arcsecond, so d / pc = 1 / (p / arcsec)) (1 pc = 3.09 × 10¹⁶ m).
items.workedSolution: From b = L / (4π d²), d = √[L / (4π b)] = 2.02 × 10¹⁷ m = 6.54 pc. Hence p = 1 / d_pc = 0.153 arcsec.

markScheme.criterion: Solves d = √[L/(4πb)] in parsecs and p = 1/d = 0.153 arcsec.

items.stem: At the summit of the circular crest of a humpback stone bridge of vertical radius 14 m, a 1180 kg vintage touring car moves horizontally at 10.1 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Determine the normal force exerted by the surface.
items.workedSolution: At the convex crest, downward resultant force is mg − N_top = m v² / R, so N_top = m(g − v²/R) = 1180 × (9.81 − (10.1)² / 14) = 2.98 × 10³ N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies radial force equation at apex to obtain 2.98 × 10³ N.

items.stem: A conical pendulum in a frictionless swivel mast consists of a 1.8 kg steel sphere and a 1.25 m inextensible string making 38 ° with the vertical axis (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Determine the orbital speed of the steel sphere.
items.workedSolution: Orbit radius r = L sin θ = 1.25 sin 38° = 0.770 m. Since T sin θ = mv²/r and T cos θ = mg, v = √(g r tan θ) = √(9.81 × 0.770 × tan 38°) = 2.43 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = L sin θ and v = √(g L sin θ tan θ) to obtain 2.43 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A 1590 kg planetary gravity-mapping orbiter around a uniform spherical planet (mass 1.16 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 6.19 × 10⁶ m) executes an elliptical Hohmann transfer with periapsis r₁ = 8.67 × 10⁶ m and apoapsis r₂ = 3.47 × 10⁷ m. Take G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². How long does the half-ellipse coast from r₁ to r₂ take?
items.workedSolution: The transfer ellipse has semi-major axis a = ½(r₁ + r₂) = 2.17 × 10⁷ m. Coasting from periapsis to apoapsis takes half an orbital period: t_H = π√(a³ / GM) = 1.14 × 10⁴ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses a = ½(r₁ + r₂) and t_H = π√(a³ / GM) to obtain 1.14 × 10⁴ s.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Averages the inner and outer half-periods linearly rather than applying T ∝ a^(3/2).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the full elliptical period 2π√(a³ / GM) instead of the half-orbit Hohmann coast time π√(a³ / GM).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses major axis (r₁ + r₂) instead of semi-major axis a = (r₁ + r₂)/2 in Kepler's third law.

items.stem: Along the 5.01 × 10⁸ m line of centres of a Pluto–Charon-type dwarf-planet binary, Dwarf Planet A (1.1 × 10²⁵ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Companion B (1.22 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) create a zero-field saddle point. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², find the total gravitational potential there.
items.workedSolution: At the zero-field point x₀ = d√M₁/(√M₁ + √M₂) = 3.76 × 10⁸ m, scalar potentials add negatively: V_g(x₀) = −GM₁/x₀ − GM₂/(d − x₀) = −(G/d)(√M₁ + √M₂)² = -2.60 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sums both negative scalar potentials at x₀ to obtain -2.60 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹.

items.stem: A radial drill shaft inside a uniform spherical cratered terrestrial dwarf planet (total mass 4.78 × 10²⁴ kg, surface radius 1.18 × 10⁷ m) stations a 250 kg polar radar surveyor at r = 6.49 × 10⁶ m from the centre. Using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², determine g(r).
items.workedSolution: Inside a uniform sphere (r < R), enclosed mass M_enc = M(r/R)³, so g(r) = G M r / R³ = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 4.78 × 10²⁴ × 6.49 × 10⁶) / (1.18 × 10⁷)³ = 1.26 N kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates gravitational field strength at r = 6.49 × 10⁶ m to obtain 1.26 N kg⁻¹.

items.stem: A cryobot instrument package of mass 803 kg is located at radial distance 3.24 × 10⁷ m from the centre of an airless icy outer-system dwarf world of mass 6.76 × 10²⁴ kg and radius 8.52 × 10⁶ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² and potential to be zero at infinity, what is the gravitational potential at the cryobot instrument package's position?
items.workedSolution: Outside the spherical mass, V_g = −G M / r = −(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 6.76 × 10²⁴) / 3.24 × 10⁷ = -1.39 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes V_g = −GM / r = -1.39 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ including the negative sign.

items.stem: Two spherical bodies in a double-planetesimal binary system — Body Alpha (9.47 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.41 × 10⁶ m) and Body Beta (1.52 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 1.57 × 10⁶ m) — lie 5.69 × 10⁸ m apart between centres. How far from Body Alpha's centre do their gravitational fields cancel?
items.workedSolution: Equating opposing field magnitudes G M₁ / x₀² = G M₂ / (d − x₀)² gives (d − x₀)/x₀ = √(M₂/M₁), so x₀ = [√M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂)] d = 4.06 × 10⁸ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses x₀ = d √M₁ / (√M₁ + √M₂) to obtain 4.06 × 10⁸ m.

items.stem: A 1580 kg alpine highway tour bus corners at 16.9 m s⁻¹ on a superelevated mountain bend of horizontal radius 58 m banked at 16 °, where the static friction coefficient is 0.4 (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed at which it can round this banked turn without skidding outward?
items.workedSolution: At maximum speed, limiting friction μ_s N acts down the slope: N(cos θ − μ_s sin θ) = mg and N(sin θ + μ_s cos θ) = m v_max² / r. Dividing yields v_max = √[g r (sin 16° + 0.4 cos 16°) / (cos 16° − 0.4 sin 16°)] = 21.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Resolves N and down-slope μ_s N horizontally and vertically to obtain v_max = 21.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Observations of a distant Coma-analog galaxy measure the ionized Calcium H absorption line at 422.2 nm compared with its laboratory reference 396.8 nm. Using v ≈ zc, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and H₀ = 66 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, find its distance in megaparsecs.
items.workedSolution: Redshift z = (λ_obs − λ₀) / λ₀ = (422.2 − 396.8) / 396.8 = 0.0640. Recession speed v ≈ z c = 1.92 × 10⁴ km s⁻¹. From Hubble's law v = H₀ d, d = v / H₀ = 1.92 × 10⁴ / 66 = 291 Mpc.

markScheme.criterion: Finds z = 0.0640, v = 1.92 × 10⁴ km s⁻¹, and d = v / H₀ = 291 Mpc.

items.stem: Above a spherical planetary body (mass 8.21 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 5.54 × 10⁶ m), a 508 kg magnetospheric plasma observatory executes uniform circular motion at altitude h = 4.16 × 10⁶ m. Taking G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², find its circular orbital speed.
items.workedSolution: Orbital radius from planet centre r = R_p + h = 5.54 × 10⁶ + 4.16 × 10⁶ = 9.7 × 10⁶ m. Equating GMm / r² = mv² / r gives v = √(GM / r) = √(6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 8.21 × 10²⁴ / 9.7 × 10⁶) = 7.51 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses r = 9.7 × 10⁶ m to obtain 7.51 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the translational kinetic energy of a 296 kg ultraviolet spectroscopy satellite in a circular orbit of radius r = 1.83 × 10⁷ m about an airless rocky planet (mass 6.32 × 10²⁴ kg, radius 8.3 × 10⁶ m, G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²).
items.workedSolution: Since m v² / r = G M m / r², orbital kinetic energy is E_k = ½ m v² = G M m / (2r) = (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 6.32 × 10²⁴ × 296) / (2 × 1.83 × 10⁷) = 3.41 × 10⁹ J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assigns a negative sign to kinetic energy by confusing E_k with total orbital energy E_tot.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses surface altitude (r − R_p) instead of orbital radius r.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 1/2 in E_k = ½mv² = GMm/(2r), computing GMm/r instead.

items.stem: On the HR diagram derived from a galactic-disc multi-band stellar census, Star Zeta-2 has photospheric temperature 4160 K and bolometric luminosity 272 L☉ (L☉ = 3.83 × 10²⁶ W, R☉ = 6.96 × 10⁸ m, σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴). Calculate R / R☉ for Star Zeta-2.
items.workedSolution: Luminosity L = 272 × 3.83 × 10²⁶ = 1.04 × 10²⁹ W. From L = 4π R² σ T⁴, R = √[L / (4π σ T⁴)] = 2.21 × 10¹⁰ m, so R / R☉ = R / (6.96 × 10⁸) = 31.7 R☉.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Stefan-Boltzmann scaling to obtain 31.7 R☉.
